data_output.description: Unchanged data.encode(splits) returns (encoded, dimension). For each split, encoded[split] is (features, labels, users), where features is int32 shape [rows, 5] in canonical source-row split order. Feature columns are exactly [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday]; hour is floor(numeric hourmin / 100) constrained to 0..23 and weekday is the calendar weekday from date with Monday=0 through Sunday=6. Vocabulary fitting remains train-only, with per-field unknown IDs and global offsets.

model_input.description: Model receives features as a rank-2 integer array of globally offset categorical IDs with exactly five IDs per row, ordered user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday. Model logits are raw float scores in the same row order. The FM logit is bias plus first-order selected-ID weights plus all pairwise second-order interactions represented by rank-16 factor embeddings.

model_designer.objective: Replace the parent additive scorer in model.py with a rank-16-capable second-order factorization-machine scorer over the unchanged five encoded categorical feature IDs.
required_changes: In model.py, change Model.__init__ to accept factor_rank in addition to dimension, learning_rate, and l2. Allocate float32 first-order weights of shape (dimension,), factor embeddings of shape (dimension, factor_rank), and a scalar bias. Initialize first-order weights and bias to zero; initialize factor embeddings reproducibly from a small zero-mean random distribution using a model-local fixed seed or an explicitly supplied seed, with finite float32 values.

Implement logits(features) as the standard second-order FM logit for exactly the feature IDs in each row: bias + sum of first-order weights for the five IDs + 0.5 * sum over latent dimensions of ((sum of the five selected factor vectors)^2 - sum of their squared factor vectors). Do not add fields, crosses, numerical features, feature aliases, or any input other than the supplied encoded IDs.

Update step(features, labels) to optimize BCE with the existing Adam optimizer family and existing learning_rate and l2 semantics. Compute gradients for both first-order weights and factor embeddings. For each selected factor vector v_i, the per-example interaction derivative is sum_selected_factors - v_i, multiplied by the BCE logit gradient. Accumulate repeated-ID gradients with np.add.at. Apply L2 regularization to first-order weights and factor embeddings, but not to bias. Maintain Adam first and second moments for every optimized parameter tensor and finite float32-compatible updates.

Keep predict(features, batch_size=200_000) returning one raw-logit score per input row in input order. Update state() and load_state() so the validation-selected checkpoint restores first-order weights, factor embeddings, and bias required for identical valid/test predictions.
preserve: Keep the data-to-model interface as a two-dimensional integer feature-ID array with one active ID per field and the existing field order [user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday].
Keep sigmoid clipping and BCE training behavior, batch prediction behavior, and no use of labels inside predict.
Do not modify data.py, train.py, or config.json; those files are owned by other agents.
coordination_notes: Trainer will pass config['factor_rank'] to Model. The required configured value is 16; do not hard-code rank 16 as a Model default in place of that configuration.
The encoded IDs are globally offset by data.encode, so a single dimension-sized first-order table and factor table are required.

The only raw fields represented by the unchanged encoder are user_id, video_id, tab, hour derived canonically as floor(numeric hourmin / 100) constrained to 0..23, and weekday derived canonically from date as Monday=0 through Sunday=6.

trainer.objective: Wire the configured rank-16 FM model into train.py and config.json while preserving validation-only checkpoint selection and emitting canonical validation and test prediction artifacts.
required_changes: In config.json, add the exact key-value pair "factor_rank": 16. Leave seed, learning_rate, l2, batch_size, max_epochs, patience, and split unchanged.
In train.py, construct Model with dimension, learning_rate=config['learning_rate'], l2=config['l2'], and factor_rank=config['factor_rank']. Do not move this configured rank into a model.py default.

Retain the existing BCE batch-training loop, training split usage, seeded train permutation, validation within_user_auc proxy, improvement threshold, patience behavior, and restoration of best_state. Select checkpoints and trigger early stopping exclusively from valid_features, valid_labels, valid_users, and validation predictions.

Do not use test labels for loss, metrics, checkpoint selection, early stopping, hyperparameter selection, or any other training decision. Only use test_features to generate final test scores after restoring the checkpoint selected on validation.

For a normal non-contract-check run, write predictions_valid.npz and predictions_test.npz in the output directory. Each file must contain exactly the two NPZ arrays row_ids and scores: predictions_valid.npz must use row_ids=np.arange(len(valid_features), dtype=np.int64) and scores=model.predict(valid_features); predictions_test.npz must use row_ids=np.arange(len(test_features), dtype=np.int64) and scores=model.predict(test_features). Preserve the encoded split row order without sorting, shuffling, grouping, or filtering predictions. If --output supplies a path, use its parent directory and ensure the validation artifact is named predictions_valid.npz.

Keep --contract-check as a finite-shape probe that instantiates the configured FM, runs one train step, and verifies one-dimensional finite validation scores; it must not train on or evaluate test labels.
preserve: Do not modify data.py or alter split boundaries, vocab fitting, categorical field order, raw input fields, BCE objective, optimizer family, or the validation-based early-stopping procedure.
Keep validation labels available only for the existing validation early-stop proxy; final ground-truth evaluation remains external to this training script.
Do not introduce additional feature families, joins, source columns, derived features, or test-informed transformations.
coordination_notes: model_designer will make Model require factor_rank and will make state/load_state include all FM parameters; pass the config value exactly.
data.encode continues to return (features, labels, users) in canonical source-row split order. Use only its features for test prediction generation and do not reference the returned test label array.
The fixed training command's non-contract execution must leave both predictions_valid.npz and predictions_test.npz present with only row_ids and scores.

reasoning: The requested ablation changes architecture only: a standard rank-16 second-order FM adds compact pairwise interactions among the already active categorical user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday IDs while retaining the first-order FM terms, BCE, split definitions, optimizer family, and validation-only early stopping. No data agent is needed because the parent encoder already uses exactly those five allowed fields with canonical hour and weekday derivations. A trainer agent is required because factor rank is a configured change and because artifact naming must be guaranteed by train.py.
